video_caption: A man with short dark hair, wearing a dark patterned collared shirt, is featured on the right side of the frame, speaking directly to the camera with a serious expression. To his left, a black, rectangular AT&T U-verse modem stands vertically, displaying the AT&T logo at the top and "AT&T U-verse" written vertically on its side, with various small indicator lights and port labels visible. Dominating the upper right portion of the screen is large white text with a black outline that reads: "Configuring your U-verse Modem". The background behind them is a dynamic, animated shot of clear turquoise and white rushing water, possibly a river or waterfall, giving a sense of movement and natural environment throughout the segment.

The video segment displays the back of a black AT&T U-verse router, held by a hand at the top left. The router has several labels with technical information. Prominently visible are "Wi-Fi Network Name: ATT8ID5UdB" and "MODEL: 5268AC FXN." Below this, there's a section for "Wi-Fi Password:" and "Device Access Code:", both of which are blurred out. An instruction reads "For Advanced Device Configuration go to: http://192.168.1.254." A yellow sticker at the bottom half reiterates the "Wi-Fi Network Name: ATT8ID5UdB" and "Wi-Fi Password:" (blurred), with "For help, att.com/support." Other details include SN, PN, MAC address, FCC compliance information, electrical rating, and "Made in China." The background shows white window blinds and some blue and white cables.

The video segment begins with a web browser open to the Google search page. In the address bar, "192.168.1.254" is typed, and a dropdown menu immediately appears below, displaying several suggested links starting with this IP address, such as "/ROX" and paths like "/PAGE=C_3_1", indicating various administrative pages or statuses. The browser then attempts to connect to the entered IP address, briefly showing "Connecting..." in the top left corner. Within a few seconds, the page transitions to the "at&t U-verse" administrative interface, identifiable by the logo at the top and navigation tabs labeled "Home," "Services," "Settings," and "Site Map," with "Home" being the active tab. The main content area of the page is titled "Key Things to Do Using Your Gateway" and lists options like "Troubleshoot," "Wi-Fi," "Restart your System," "Home Network," and "Customize Firewall," each with a brief explanatory text. Below this, a "Gateway Status" section displays details such as "Connection to AT&T: Up," "Battery: Battery is not present," and "Wi-Fi" information including "2.4 GHz Radio Status: Up," "Network Name (SSID): ATTBD500," and "Type: User." Buttons like "Refresh Page," "Restart," and "More Info" are also visible on the interface.

The video segment displays a web browser window, likely Google Chrome, showing the interface for an AT&T U-verse gateway. In the address bar, the IP address "192.168.1.254" is visible, indicating a local network access. Several tabs are open, including "Home," "ASUS Login," "how do I log out of my u...", and "How to log into an AT&T +...", suggesting the user is managing or researching router settings. The main content area shows the AT&T U-verse logo at the top, followed by navigation tabs: "Home," "Services," "Settings," and "Site Map," with "Home" currently selected. A section titled "Key Things to do Using Your Gateway" lists options like "Troubleshoot," "Wi-Fi," "Restart your System," "Home Network," and "Customize Firewall," each with a brief description and a "Refresh Page" button. Below this, a "Gateway Status" section provides information: "Connection to AT&T" is "Up" with a "Restart" button, "Battery" states "Battery is not present," and "Wi-Fi" shows "2.4 GHz Radio Status" with a "Restart" button, "Network name (SSID)" as "ATT8iDSUDb," and "Type" as "User," along with a "More Info" button. A white mouse cursor is visible in the bottom right corner of the browser window, outside the page content.

The video segment opens on a computer screen displaying a web browser with multiple tabs, including one labeled "192.168.1.254", "ASUS Login", and "How do I log out of my u..." (likely U-verse). The active tab shows the "AT&T U-verse" router configuration page, with "Settings" as the selected main tab. Within the "Settings" tab, "System Info" is initially highlighted, but the cursor swiftly clicks on the "LAN" sub-tab at 0:01, transitioning the view to "LAN Status" information. Immediately after, the cursor clicks on the "DHCP" sub-tab at 0:01, which loads the "LAN DHCP Configuration" page. A warning banner states: "Warning: Modifying the settings on this page can impact the ability of devices to access your private network." The "DHCP Configuration" section displays "DHCP Network Range" options, with radio buttons for default ranges and "Configure manually". The cursor clicks the "Configure manually" radio button. The user then proceeds to manually input network details: "192.168.1.254" into the "Router Address" field, "255.255.255.0" into the "Subnet Mask" field, "192.168.1.1" into the "First DHCP Address" field, and "192.168.1.1" into the "Last DHCP Address" field, effectively restricting the DHCP range to a single IP. The "DHCP Lease Time" is set to "24 hours (24 hours default)". The screen then scrolls down to reveal the "Guest DHCP Configuration" section, which also has a "Configure manually" option and input fields, though no entries are made there. Finally, the cursor clicks the "Save" button at the bottom of the page at 0:01. After saving, the video shows the user clicking the "Firewall" sub-tab within "Settings".

The video displays a web browser window showing the AT&T U-verse router configuration page, specifically under the "Settings" tab. Initially, the "Firewall" tab is selected, and the user clicks on the "Applications, Pinholes and DMZ" sub-tab. On this page, titled "Allow device application traffic to pass through firewall," the user enters "192.168.1.1" into the "Enter IP address" field under "1) Select a computer" and clicks "Choose." After the page refreshes, the user scrolls down and clicks the "Save" button. Subsequently, the user navigates back to the main tabs and clicks on the "LAN" tab, then selects the "Wi-Fi" sub-tab. A warning message appears: "Warning: Modifying the settings on this page can impact the ability of devices to access your wireless network." (Warning: Modifying the settings on this page can impact the ability of devices to access your wireless network.) The user proceeds to disable both the "2.4 GHz Wi-Fi Interface" and the "5 GHz Wi-Fi Interface" by selecting "Disabled" from their respective dropdown menus. Finally, the user scrolls down the page and clicks the "Save" button to apply these changes.

The video segment opens with a computer screen displaying an AT&T U-verse modem/router configuration page, showing Wi-Fi settings for a 2.4 GHz radio, including options for Wi-Fi interface, channel, and frequency, along with a warning about modifying settings. The browser tabs indicate related searches about AT&T and an ASUS login. The scene then shifts to a physical white ASUS RT-N16 router with blue indicator lights, sitting on a wooden surface. A close-up shot reveals the router's label, detailing its model name, power input, and "Factory Default settings" including the IP Address "192.168.2.1" and blurred username and password fields, highlighted by a yellow Pac-Man icon. The video returns to the computer screen, showing a Google search page where the user types "192.168.2.1" into the browser's address bar, and then navigates to the ASUS login page. This login screen displays "SIGN IN RT-N16" with blurred username and password fields, and a red "Invalid username or password" message, before the user clicks "Sign in". The screen quickly transitions to the ASUS Wireless Router's administrative interface, showing system status, network map, and various settings, confirming the "Operation Mode: Wireless router" and the "LAN IP: 192.168.2.1".

In this segment, a browser window displays an ASUS wireless router configuration page. On the left sidebar, the "WAN" link under "Advanced Settings" is highlighted in blue. The main content area shows "WAN - Internet Connection" with "Basic Config" options. The user clicks on the dropdown for "WAN Connection Type," changes it from "Automatic IP" to "Static IP," and then proceeds to manually enter network details. For "IP Address," they type "192.168.1.1"; for "Subnet Mask," they input "255.255.255.0"; and for "Default Gateway" and "DNS Server1," they enter "192.168.1.254." After filling in these details, the user clicks the "Apply" button at the bottom of the page, causing a brief loading animation. Once the settings are applied, the user navigates to the "LAN" section by clicking the corresponding link in the left sidebar, revealing the "LAN - LAN IP" configuration page where the "IP Address" is shown as "192.168.2.1" and "Subnet Mask" as "255.255.255.0."

A computer screen displays a web browser showing the "Wi-Fi configuration" page for an ASUS RT-N16 wireless router, with the URL `192.168.2.1/Advanced_LAN_Content.asp` visible in the address bar. The router's web interface is open to the "LAN - LAN IP" settings page. The main section of the page, titled "LAN - LAN IP," shows fields for "IP Address" and "Subnet Mask." The "IP Address" field contains "192.168.2.1" and is highlighted, while the "Subnet Mask" field contains "255.255.255.0". A dark gray "Apply" button is centered below these fields, and the mouse cursor hovers over it. On the left side, a navigation menu has "LAN" highlighted under "Advanced Settings." The top of the router interface displays "ASUS RT-N16," along with "Logout," "Reboot," and an "English" language selection. Information below this includes "Operation Mode: wireless router," "Firmware Version: 9.0.0.4.180.2985," and "SSID: Elias." The browser itself has several tabs open at the top and various browser extensions visible in the toolbar.

The video opens with a close-up of a computer screen displaying an ASUS Wireless Router RT-N16 configuration page, showing options like "LAN - LAN IP" with an IP Address of "192.168.2.1" and a Subnet Mask of "255.255.255.0", and various menu items on the left side, such as "Quick Internet Setup", "Network Map", and "Advanced Settings". At 0:04, the screen partially transitions to reveal a man with short dark hair and a dark blue collared shirt on the right side, speaking directly to the camera with a neutral expression. Behind him and partially over the computer screen, a scenic background of a river flowing over smooth, grey rocks is superimposed. A black AT&T U-verse modem appears on the left side, next to the man, and a white title "Configuring your U-verse Modem" is prominently displayed in the center. The man continues to speak, and at 0:10, the video fades to a white screen, which then displays several lines of black text, including "Thanks for watching this tutorial." and "Please, like and subscribe!" followed by disclaimers about liability, accuracy, and usage rights, and credits for background music and video clips: "The logos and trademarks shown on this video are the properties of their respective owners. I am in no way liable for the misuse of the content in this video. I cannot guarantee the accuracy of any of the information contained here. Use it at your own risk. This video can be freely shared, copied and reused in any way you see fit. This video should not be sold individually or as part of a package. It must be freely shared. A special thanks goes to Stephen Richards (longzijun) for his talent and his selflessness in sharing his music that was used on the background. A special thanks also goes to Ketil Bjornstad and David Darling for sharing their beautiful video clip on Vimeo entitled "THE RIVER - flows in your head" that was used on the background of this video. Just remember to give credit where credit is due." These credits remain on screen until the end of the segment.
